stories.headline: SK Hynix to spend 1 billion dollars over five years to support chip suppliers
stories.script: Our lead story today. SK Hynix said on Monday it will invest 1.4 trillion won, or 1.05 billion dollars , across the next five years to back South Korean suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, The Economic Times reports. The chipmaker wants a sturdier supply chain as rivalry in the industry grows.

He said companies and governments must get workers ready as the nature of work shifts.

stories.headline: upGrad Enters Enterprise Advisory With Launch Of upGrad Next
stories.script: Turning to India. Edtech unicorn upGrad has launched upGrad Next, a new enterprise advisory practice, Inc42 reports. The unit pairs consulting with the company's current skilling and recruitment services. It will counsel senior executives on how organisations are structured, along with hiring, pay and workforce development, as businesses get staff ready for AI. upGrad can then help clients carry out those changes. Four former Deloitte and EY executives will run the practice as managing directors, and further senior leaders are expected to join over the next few weeks.
stories.whyThisMatters: Edtech unicorn upGrad has launched upGrad Next, a new enterprise advisory practice, Inc42 reports.

stories.headline: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence
stories.script: Also today. European militaries are looking for alternatives to Palantir to reduce reliance on the United States, The Economic Times reports. Last week, Germany's Helsing introduced Clarity, a military intelligence software product. Such AI systems speed up military decisions by combing through large volumes of data to flag threats and suggest responses, including targeting and strikes.
stories.whyThisMatters: European militaries are looking for alternatives to Palantir to reduce reliance on the United States, The Economic Times reports.
keyPoints: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence

stories.headline: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
stories.script: From the research desk. A new research paper, titled Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems, argues that robotics has entered a different phase. The researchers say the arrival of GPT-6 Astra kicked off what they call agentic robotics. Within a few weeks, large frontier models wrapped in agent software equalled or beat specialised robot controllers on many physical-world tests. Rather than training a separate system for each group of tasks, one foundation model handles open-ended jobs in a continuous cycle. It watches its surroundings, works out what the user wants, plans, uses skills and tools, checks results and adjusts. The researchers note the field still lacks an agreed definition, a dependable way to measure progress and a plan for future research.
stories.whyThisMatters: A new research paper, titled Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems, argues that robotics has entered a different phase.
keyPoints: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
